Getting Started

Turn your MAP data into a plan in under a minute

No sign-in, no setup. Upload your NWEA ASG export, plus the Class Profile export for each subject, and this dashboard instantly shows who grew, who needs support, who closed gaps, and how to group your class — all in your browser. Uploading in the fall with only one test window? The dashboard detects that and switches to a start-of-year view with tiers, norm placement and growth targets instead of showing empty growth panels.

Prefer a manual? Download the user guide (PDF) — every section explained, with pictures. The ? in the corner of each section explains it in place.

  1. 1
    Export two reports from NWEA MAP The ASG (Achievement Status & Growth) report for your class, and the Class Profile report for each subject, both as CSV. Same class, same term, every student in both. In the fall, a single-term export works too.
  2. 2
    Upload it here Drag the file onto the upload box, or click to browse. Your data stays on your device.
  3. 3
    Plan with confidence Explore growth, gap closure, priority & celebration lists, then build seating groups and export or print.
Which files do I export, and what does this tool read?
Exporting from NWEA MAP Growth — you need both
  1. Sign in to MAP Growth and open MAP Reports.
  2. Run the Achievement Status and Growth (ASG) report for your class and terms, and download it as CSV. This file carries growth.
  3. Run the Class Profile report for the same class and term, once per subject, and download each as CSV. These files carry the instructional areas inside each subject.
  4. Return here and upload all of them together — nothing is sent anywhere.

Get both right. Same class, same term, every student in both. The dashboard folds each student's ASG record and Class Profile record into one. If the two exports disagree about a student's score, the Data Check names the student and both figures: check the exports rather than trust either number for that student.

Good to know
  • Column names are matched automatically, so slightly different exports still work. Comma, semicolon and tab separated files are all read.
  • Suppressed values (***) and missing scores are handled gracefully.
  • Fall uploads with no prior window are fully supported. When the export has a single test window the dashboard hides the growth, gap-closure and quadrant panels — which would only show blanks — and analyses the window it has: percentile distribution, instructional tiers, distance from the US grade and season norm, and RIT targets for the rest of the year. It does not matter whether your export puts the fall test in the Start or the End columns.
  • An ASG file on its own gives you everything except the instructional areas; Class Profile files on their own give you the areas and a single window, but no growth. Load both for the whole picture.
  • Nothing is persisted. Only your theme and motion preferences are remembered; no student data is ever written to disk or sent anywhere.
  • Not ready to export? Click Load Sample Data to explore every feature first, with a made-up grade 5 and 6 cohort loaded the way yours would be: an ASG export and a Class Profile export together.

Distributions

Every record as a dot over a box for the middle half, one row per subject. An average hides the shape of a group; this shows it.

Growth and Achievement

Uses NWEA growth/achievement quadrants when present, with an overall view and a subject breakdown.

What the quadrants mean NWEA reports three levels on each axis, not two, and this dashboard keeps all three. A student scored average growth and average achievement is on track — not low on both, which is what folding average in with low would say about them.
Why this matters This separates achievement from growth, so a lower-scoring student with strong growth is not treated the same as a lower-scoring student with low growth.
How to read movement Improved, declined, and stayed same compare StartGrowthandAchievement to EndGrowthandAchievement for the same student-subject record.

Growth by starting band

Whether this group grew its lowest starters as well as its highest. A class average can look healthy while one end of the roster stands still.

Movement

Gap Closure

Secure benchmark: 61st percentile. Overall cards are followed by subject-level gap patterns.

For students below 61 Gap closure measures how much of the distance to the secure benchmark was closed from start to end percentile.
For students at 61+ The dashboard checks whether secure students extended, maintained, regressed, or dropped below the secure benchmark.
Band movement Moved up or moved down compares the start and end percentile color bands for each student-subject record.

Instructional Areas

Where the strengths and gaps sit inside each subject.

What an area score is A RIT for one strand of the test, built from a fraction of the items. NWEA publishes no percentile and no norm for an area, so it cannot be read on its own.
So everything here is relative Each area is compared with the same student's overall RIT on the same test. “Below” means below their own level, not below grade level — which is why each subject also states where the group sits against the US norm. A flat profile can mean evenly behind.
Class patterns are the reliable part Averaging across the class shrinks the measurement error, so a class-level gap is trustworthy where a single student's area score is not.
How a student is flagged Only when their area sits far enough from their own overall RIT to be larger than the measurement error in this file.
By subject

Each bar is the class mean difference between that area and the students' own overall RIT, with its 95% confidence interval. An area is only named as a pattern when the interval clears zero.

Ready-made teaching groups

Students whose score in one area sits clearly below the rest of what they can do in that subject. This is a strand to reteach in a small group, not a reason to move a student down a set.

Wall Posters

Data stories for the classroom wall, sized for A3, in sections: the whole class first, then one section per subject. The subject sections are selected to start; tick the whole-class section to add the combined set. Class-level only — no student is named and no individual score appears.

Written for students, not for you Each poster says one thing a student can act on, in language they can read. The method notes stay in the dashboard.
Nobody is named Every figure is a class total, share or median. A poster on a wall is seen by visitors, so no name, no individual score and no rank appears on one.
They follow your filters Filter to one class or one subject and the posters describe that group. The footer of each poster records which group it came from.
Printing One poster per page, in A3 or A4, landscape or portrait. In the print dialog set the paper size to match, margins to none, scale to 100%, and turn on background graphics.
Optional. Use the class name the students know.
